title: Amendment 3: No Post-Conviction Bail for Aggravated Offenses Against a Minor

context.text: Referred to the ballot by the Louisiana Legislature as House Bill 51 (Act 271), sponsored by Rep. Debbie Villio (R); amendments require a two-thirds vote of each chamber and no gubernatorial signature. The House passed it 92-0 and the Senate 31-1 (per the bill history).

question.text: Do you support an amendment to prohibit a defendant from being released on any post-conviction bail if the defendant is convicted of an aggravated offense against a minor child? (Adds Article I, Section 18(C))

summary.text: The amendment adds Article I, Section 18(C) to the Louisiana Constitution: after conviction, a person is not bailable if the offense is an aggravated offense, as defined by R.S. 15:541, committed against a victim who is a minor. Current law lets a person be bailable after conviction in some circumstances depending on the maximum or imposed sentence (five years or less). Fiscal impact (Legislative Fiscal Office): an "indeterminable increase" in local sheriffs' expenditures, because people convicted of such offenses would be held in parish jails rather than released on bail; no direct material effect on governmental revenues.

measure.yesMeans: Adds to the Constitution a bar on any post-conviction bail for a person convicted of an aggravated offense, as defined in state law, committed against a minor.
measure.noMeans: Leaves the Constitution's bail provisions unchanged, so post-conviction bail for such offenses remains governed by the existing rules.

researchNotes: Ballot question text is the proposition printed in the enrolled joint resolution, which directs that it be placed on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot; vote counts, Act numbers and fiscal information are from the Louisiana Legislature's bill pages, résumé digests and Legislative Fiscal Office notes. The Louisiana Secretary of State's certified list could not be loaded (sos.la.gov election pages returned 404 on Oct 19, 2026), so the Amendment 1-10 numbering and the question wording were checked against the nonpartisan PAR Guide to the Fall 2026 Constitutional Amendments, which lists the same ten amendments in the same order with the same question text; the parenthetical effective-date and constitutional-citation text follows the enrolled resolution. Louisiana has no citizen initiative and publishes no voter-pamphlet arguments; a majority of votes cast approves an amendment. No supporting or opposing arguments or campaign committees were found in the sources reviewed.
